newsitem.title: UK: More British coal pits face closure - lobby group.
newsitem.headline: More British coal pits face closure - lobby group.

text.p: More than half of Britain's remaining 29 coal pits face closure within the next five years if coal continues to lose out to gas as the preferred fuel for new power plants, a lobby group said on Monday.

In a report entitled "A fair deal for coal: a fair deal for Britain", the Coalfields Community Campaign (CCC) said only 10 to 12 colleries would survive, and 10,000 jobs would be lost if no prompt action was taken.
"A new Labour government must be made aware of the seriousness of the distortions that still exist in the energy market," CCC chairman Bill Flanagan said at the presentation of the report.
The report calls for an inquiry into supply agreements between regional electricity companies (RECs) and gas-fired power generators, which the RECs helped to build in the early 1990s.
These agreements, the CCC claims, lead to expensive electricity, while at the same time locking out the coal industry from the power market.
The CCC also wants tougher controls on the licensing of new gas-fired stations and is demanding a public review of the costs of running Britain's oldest nuclear stations.
"Coal is excluded from much of its main power station market by a combination of subsidised nuclear power and anti-competitive contracts for gas," the CCC said in a statement.
